Nov 9, 2026

Partitioned cookie support for Bot Management

Bots

Cloudflare now adds the Partitioned attribute to the __cf_bm cookie on compatible HTTPS requests. The attribute is added only when the cookie can also be issued with SameSite=None and Secure.

When users access your content through an <iframe> on another site, the browser handles __cf_bm as a third-party cookie. Browser privacy controls may block third-party cookies. Adding Partitioned allows the __cf_bm cookie to persist within that top-level site. This means that Bot Management can preserve continuity across requests, even when your content is embedded on another site.

For more information, refer to Cloudflare cookies.

Nov 4, 2026

Granular access controls for the top Personal Agents

Bots

The Configure AI bot policies setting is now named AI Crawler and Agent access policies.

Personal agents act on a person's behalf, fetching information or browsing in response to a request. The updated policies let you set actions for the top Personal Agents individually. This gives you control over agent access while allowing visitors to use agents to find answers or compare products using your site's content.

Customize how Personal Agents access your site via Security > Settings > AI Crawler and Agent access policies.

For more information, check out our blog ↗︎ or refer to our documentation for AI Crawler and Agent access policies.

Nov 3, 2026

See which AI assistants act for your users in Account Abuse Protection

Bots

Account Abuse Protection now shows when a recognized AI assistant makes a login or sign up request, and which account it was acting for.

  • Population overview: See which AI assistants are active across your users and how many accounts use them.
  • Account activity: Every login and sign up event shows whether an AI assistant made the request, and which one.
  • AI assistant filters: filter accounts by number of AI assistant events or number of AI assistants.

Use this to investigate and mitigate a single account without blocking an assistant for everyone else who relies on it, and to tune your agent settings in AI Crawler and Agent access policies.

AI assistant visibility covers login and sign up events only. Requests from assistants that Cloudflare does not recognize appear as ordinary traffic.

For more information, refer to AI assistants.

Nov 2, 2026

New Account Abuse Protection Dashboard

Bots

Account Abuse Protection customers in Early Access can now investigate login and sign up activity in a dedicated dashboard under Security > Account Abuse Protection.

  • Population overview: See total login and sign up events, unique accounts, IPs and devices, top countries and ASNs, and leaked credential check results. Filter accounts by signals such as leaked credential events and unique IPs to find the accounts that need review.
  • Individual Account overview: Review a single Hashed User ID's activity, including its top networks, locations and devices, and an event log with the Ray ID for each event. Mitigate the account with a Security Rule on its Hashed User ID.
  • New roles: The Account Abuse Protection role grants access to the dashboard. Account Abuse Protection PII role grants access to the dashboard as well as account-level PII, such as email address, and is required to create or edit Logpush jobs that include PII. The dashboard includes all login and sign up events from the date the feature was enabled.

For more information, refer to Account Abuse Protection.

Oct 30, 2026

Workers subrequests now preserve context for BYOIP destinations

WorkersBYOIPBots

Cloudflare now preserves Workers context when a subrequest targets a Cloudflare-proxied hostname using Bring Your Own IP (BYOIP). These requests are identified as Cloudflare-to-Cloudflare traffic instead of external Internet traffic.

Previously, some BYOIP subrequests could lose Workers context and original client signals. This could cause security rules to behave unexpectedly, Bot Management to evaluate an internal Cloudflare connection instead of the original client, or affected requests to return false 403 responses.

Workers subrequests to BYOIP destinations now preserve the CF-Worker header and cf.worker.upstream_zone field. This supports consistent security rule evaluation across same-zone and cross-zone subrequests.

Bot Management fields on the destination zone now represent the original end-user connection for affected BYOIP subrequests. Bot scores, verified bot status, and JA3/JA4 fingerprints no longer represent the internal connection between Cloudflare services.

Because Cloudflare-proxied BYOIP destinations now follow standard Workers subrequest handling, cross-zone requests set CF-Connecting-IP to the Workers client IP address 2a06:98c0:3600::103 for security reasons. This applies when a Worker in one Cloudflare zone sends a subrequest to a hostname in another Cloudflare zone. Same-zone subrequests continue to reflect the client IP through CF-Connecting-IP.

For more information, refer to Cloudflare BYOIP, Workers subrequests, and CF-Connecting-IP in Worker subrequests.

Oct 28, 2026

China-native Challenge Pages for the China Network

China NetworkChallengesBots

Challenge Pages served through the Cloudflare China Network now use Turnstile widgets hosted in Mainland China. This means that visitors in Mainland China can complete challenges faster and more reliably because widgets no longer need to make cross-border requests.

You do not need to take any action: this change applies automatically when a China Network zone presents a Challenge Page. Visitors served by Cloudflare's global network will continue to receive the global Challenge Page experience.

For more information, refer to Interstitial Challenge Pages and Cloudflare China Network.

Oct 19, 2026

Precursor adds Monitor mode

Bots

We released Monitor mode at customers' request so they can test Precursor and the Precursor Interstitial without updating bot score.

In Security > Settings, the Precursor Status dropdown now offers Off, Monitor, and Arm. Selecting Arm means Precursor detections can affect bot score and Challenge clearance. Selecting Monitor means Precursor detections do not affect bot score or Challenge clearance.

We also separated the Precursor Interstitial from the mode. Set the sitewide default with Show Interstitial, then add Interstitial Rules to customize it for specific requests. For example, leave Show Interstitial off across most of your site, but require an interstitial Challenge on /checkout to enforce a valid session before purchase.

For more information, refer to the Precursor documentation.

Sep 16, 2026

Control JavaScript Detections API results

Bots

Enterprise Bot Management customers can control whether Cloudflare uses results created through the JavaScript Detections API for bot scoring and detections.

Turn JavaScript Detections for API traffic on or off in Security > Settings. You can also configure the zone through the Bot Management API by setting jsd_api_results_enabled:

This setting is separate from zone-wide script injection. When it is off, the API script can still execute and return success to the callback, but Cloudflare does not consume the result.

For more information, refer to JavaScript Detections.

Aug 31, 2026

Bot Management's machine learning model now retrains more frequently instead of shipping fixed versions

Bots

We have launched Adaptive Intelligence, a new bot detection engine built to close the gap between when an attack pattern first appears and when protection against it reaches every customer. You can read the announcement blog ↗︎ for the full story behind why we built it.

Adaptive Intelligence, the machine learning model behind your bot score, now retrains more frequently instead of shipping as a fixed, numbered version. As new bypass tools and bot frameworks appear, the model learns from them and folds that knowledge in without waiting for a scheduled release.

Every update is validated before it affects you. New model versions run in shadow mode first, scored but not acted on, and are compared against the current model before rolling out gradually.

Enterprise customers with Auto-update machine learning switched on under Bot Management configurations get Adaptive Intelligence automatically, with no version to migrate and nothing else to configure.

To learn more, refer to Adaptive Intelligence and Machine Learning models.

Jul 13, 2026

Precursor introduces session-based bot detection

Bots

Precursor is rolling out to all customers starting today. Precursor is client-side JavaScript that enables session-based bot detection.

You can read the announcement blog ↗︎ for background on why we built Precursor and how session-level behavioral detection works.

With Precursor enabled, Cloudflare can:

  • Continuously evaluate behavioral signals across a session
  • Re-validate challenge clearance as behavior changes
  • Update bot scores with session context
  • Provide client-side visibility where none previously existed

It integrates with existing protections, including Security Rules, and can be enabled directly from the Cloudflare dashboard with configurable modes to balance security and user experience.

To learn more, refer to the Precursor documentation.

Jul 1, 2026

New options to manage AI traffic

Bots

Not all AI traffic is the same. Now, all customers — including those on the Free plan — can manage AI crawlers based on what they actually do on your site. Cloudflare groups AI traffic into three behaviors you can control independently: Search, Agent, and Training. This lets you keep the automated traffic that sends readers and revenue back to you, while blocking the traffic that only takes from your content.

Each behavior maps to a real use case. Search covers crawlers that index your content so they can answer questions about it later, where you should expect referral traffic or other equitable compensation in return. Agent covers automated activity acting in real time on a person's behalf, such as chat fetch bots and browser-use agents. Training covers crawlers that take your content to train or fine-tune a model. For each preset you can choose to block on all pages, block only on pages that display ads, or choose not to block.

Starting September 15, 2026, new domains onboarding to Cloudflare receive updated defaults: Bots classified as Training or as Agent are blocked on pages that display ads, while Search remains allowed. On that date, multi-purpose crawlers that combine Search and Training will be affected by the new defaults to block Training. All customers can opt out of the new defaults ↗︎ at any time before September 15.

Jul 1, 2026

More visibility into bot traffic with BotBase and Business Insights

Bots

With Content Independence Day 2026, Enterprise Bot Management customers get two new tools that make bot traffic far easier to see and reason about: BotBase, a searchable directory of every bot Cloudflare tracks, and Business Insights, a dashboard that shows how much value each crawler sends back to your business.

BotBase is Cloudflare's directory of all known bots and agents, available directly in the dashboard. It shows how Cloudflare classifies each bot by behavior — Search, Agent, Training, and other categories such as Transact, Data Collection, SEO, and Ads Verification — so you can understand why a given crawler is visiting you. You can search and filter the full catalogue, filter your own traffic down to a single bot to investigate its activity on your zone, and copy any bot's detection ID to target it precisely in Security rules. Every tracked bot in BotBase is also published in Cloudflare Radar's bots and agents directory ↗︎.

Business Insights is built for content owners and business decision-makers who want to know which bots help or harm their business, without reading rule syntax. The dashboard reports crawl-to-referral ratios both site-wide and per bot operator — comparing how often a company crawls your content against how many visitors it actually refers back — over the last 24 hours, 7 days, or 30 days. Each operator is labeled with Cloudflare's updated classification and an action status of Allowed, Blocked, or Partially blocked, giving stakeholders a shared, at-a-glance view of the AI traffic reaching your site.
